senses.gloss:
Kṣviṅkā is mentioned once in the Rigveda as a bird of prey. The word also occurs in the list of victims at the aśvamedha, or horse sacrifice, in the taittirīya Saṃhitā, where the commentary absurdly explains it as ‘a red-mouthed female ape’ (rakta-mukhī vānarī).
Foot notes x. 87, 7.
v. 5, 15, 1.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 93.
